title: Which number do we multiply by to divide?
description: Two thirds divided by three fifths is worked out with a quicker rule. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, which has the numerator and denominator interchanged. Keeko raises the doubt of taking the reciprocal of the wrong fraction.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. Watch for students who take the reciprocal of the dividend instead of the divisor.

video_script.why: A learner turns the two small steps of the earlier videos into one quick rule with a name.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own rule, two thirds and three fifths
video_script.anchor: two thirds divided by three fifths, with the reciprocal of three fifths written beside it
video_script.wrong_move: takes the reciprocal of the dividend instead of the divisor
video_script.payoff_line: Two thirds divided by three fifths is ten ninths
video_script.fraction_reading: two thirds, three fifths, five thirds, three halves, ten ninths, nine tenths
maths_rules: the reciprocal of a fraction has its numerator and denominator interchanged
dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal
the slip: 3/2 × 3/5 = 9/10, which uses the reciprocal of the dividend
video_script.design: The divisor is shown with its numerator and denominator interchanged, and the dividend is multiplied by the result.

<bookmark mark='pose'/>Find two thirds divided by three fifths, with that rule.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is two thirds divided by three fifths?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.prod: three fifths times five thirds is written with the product one
marks.name: five thirds is labelled with the word reciprocal

narration: <bookmark mark='prod'/>Three fifths times five thirds comes to one.
<bookmark mark='name'/>We call five thirds the reciprocal of three fifths.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>To write a reciprocal, interchange the numerator and the denominator.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find two thirds divided by three fifths.

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step one, the divisor is three fifths, the number we divide by.
<bookmark mark='recip'/>Its reciprocal is five thirds.

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, multiply the dividend, two thirds, by that reciprocal.
<bookmark mark='tb'/>That is two times five on top, over three times three.

beats.on_screen: 2, 5, 3 and 3 share no common factor, so nothing is shortened

marks.look: each top is checked against each bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='look'/>Step three, check each top against each bottom.
<bookmark mark='tick'/>No top shares a factor with a bottom, so nothing can be shortened.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Two thirds divided by three fifths is ten ninths.
That is one and one ninth.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 3/2 × 3/5 = 9/10; the divisor 3/5 is outlined and its reciprocal 5/3 is shown instead

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the reciprocal of the dividend
marks.fix: the divisor is outlined and its reciprocal is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we take the reciprocal of two thirds, which gives an answer of nine tenths.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>But the reciprocal belongs to the divisor, the number we divide by.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Three fifths is the divisor, so five thirds is the reciprocal we multiply by.
